title: 的 (de) in Chinese: HSK 1 Grammar with Examples
description: How to use 的 (de) in Chinese: my, your and whose, when to leave 的 out, describing nouns with 的, and "mine" or "the big one", with HSK 1 examples.
h1: How to Use 的 (de) for Possession and Description
lede: 的 (de) links a word or phrase to the noun that comes after it. It works like 's in "the teacher's car", and it also joins a description to a noun. It is one of the most common characters in Chinese and a core grammar point of HSK 1.

paras: Put 的 after a person or pronoun to show that something belongs to them. 我的 is "my", 你的 is "your", 他的 is "his" and 老师的 is "the teacher's". To ask "whose?", use 谁的. 的 always has a light, neutral tone.

examples.py: Zhè shì wǒ gēge de chē.
examples.en: This is my older brother's car.

examples.py: Wǒ péngyou de māma shì lǎoshī.
examples.en: My friend's mum is a teacher.

sections.h2: When you can leave 的 out
paras: After a pronoun such as 我, 你, 他 or 我们, 的 is usually dropped before family members, close relationships and places you belong to, such as your school or company. Chinese speakers say 我妈妈, not 我的妈妈, although 我的妈妈 is not wrong.
In other cases, keep 的. 我的手机 is correct; 我手机 is heard in casual speech, but as a learner you are safer with 的.
的 also joins a description to a noun. The description always comes before the noun, even when English puts it after: "the apples I bought" is 我买的苹果, literally "I bought 的 apples".
A one-syllable adjective usually goes straight onto the noun without 的: 新手机, 好朋友. When the adjective has 很 in front of it, or the description is longer, you need 的.

examples.py: Wǒ xiǎng mǎi yí ge xīn shǒujī.
examples.en: I want to buy a new phone.

examples.py: Tā shì yí ge hěn hǎo de lǎoshī.
examples.en: He is a very good teacher.

examples.py: Wǒ mǎi de píngguǒ hěn hǎochī.
examples.en: The apples I bought are delicious.

examples.zh: 你昨天看的电影怎么样？
examples.py: Nǐ zuótiān kàn de diànyǐng zěnmeyàng?
examples.en: How was the film you saw yesterday?

examples.py: Wǒ xǐhuan chī māma zuò de fàn.

sections.h2: Leaving out the noun: "mine" and "the big one"
paras: If everyone already knows which thing you mean, you can drop the noun and end with 的. 我的 then means "mine", 谁的 means "whose", and 大的 means "the big one".

examples.py: Zhè běn shū shì wǒ de.

paras: Learners often forget 的 after 很 + adjective. 很好老师 is wrong; say 很好的老师. Without 很, 好老师 is fine.

The other mistake is putting the description after the noun, as in English. In Chinese, whatever describes the noun, whether it is an owner, an adjective or a whole phrase, comes first, then 的, then the noun.

worksheet.title: 的 (de) Worksheet: HSK 1 Printable with Answers
worksheet.description: A free printable 的 (de) worksheet for HSK 1: 20 exercises (choose 的 or 是, word order, fix the mistake) with an answer key.

exercises.instructions: Write 的 or 是 in each gap. The English tells you what the sentence means.

items.en: This is my friend's computer.
My teacher is very nice.
Whose phone is that?
He is my classmate.
She is a very good doctor.
Is this cup yours?
Where is the book you bought yesterday?
I'd like the small one.

exercises.instructions: Write the words as one correct sentence.

items.en: This is the teacher's book.
The food Mum cooks is delicious.
He is a very good friend of mine.
The film we watched yesterday was very good.
answers: 我们昨天看的电影很好看。
昨天我们看的电影很好看。

items.en: That computer is mine.
My classmate's dad is a doctor.

exercises.instructions: Each sentence has one mistake. Write the correct sentence.

items.en: This is a very big shop.
I like the clothes you bought.
Whose computer is that?
This phone is mine.

items.zh: 他有一个很漂亮女朋友。
items.en: He has a very pretty girlfriend.
answers: 他有一个很漂亮的女朋友。

items.en: The clothes I bought yesterday look nice.
answers: 我昨天买的衣服很好看。
